variants.when: Cars with a menu on the center screen (seen in 2016, 2021 and 2024 owner's manuals; the menu is called Vehicle Info on older cars and My MINI on newer ones)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the sticker in the driver's door opening.
Start the engine but do not drive off.
On the center screen, open Vehicle Info or My MINI, then Vehicle status, then Tire Pressure Monitor.
Drive away. The new pressures are saved by themselves after several minutes of driving, and the reset resumes if you stop partway.
variants.note: If the tire light flashes and then stays on, the system cannot watch the tires. Try the reset once more; if it keeps happening, have the system checked.

variants.when: Older cars set from the button on the end of the turn signal lever (seen in 2008 Hardtop and 2016 Countryman and Paceman owner's manuals)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the sticker in the driver's door opening.
Start the engine but stay parked.
Tap the button on the end of the turn signal lever until SET/INFO shows, then press and hold it until the display changes.
Tap the button until the tire symbol shows with RESET, then press and hold it until the display changes.
Drive off. The system finishes while you drive; on cars with wheel sensors this takes a short drive above about 20 mph.
variants.note: Do not reset with snow chains on or with a space-saver spare fitted. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.

notes: MINI owner's manuals show the service reminders (for example under Vehicle status, Service required) but give no driver reset for the oil service reminder; they say a service advisor reads the service data from the key. So only the tire pressure reset is listed. Reset the tire monitor after every pressure change and after any tire or wheel change.
